chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of our companions, raising it (to the Imam), said:

I asked him about how the woman would be enshrouded. So he said: 'Just as the man would be enshrouded, apart from that a cloth would be tightened upon her breasts to press the breasts upon the chest and it would be tightened upon her back, and the cotton (padding) would be done for her more than what would be done for the man, and stuffing the front and the back with the cotton and the embalming (camphor), then the cloth would be tightened upon her with an intense tightening'.

key_terms.تُكَفَّنُ: to be enshrouded (in the burial shroud)
key_terms.خِرْقَةٌ: a piece of cloth or rag used for binding

ai.seo_question: What are the specific differences in how a woman is enshrouded compared to a man according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual rulings for enshrouding a deceased woman, distinguishing it from men by mandating a binding cloth over the breasts to keep them close to the chest, increased cotton padding, and stuffing the front and rear with cotton and camphor (hanoot). Scholarly tradition emphasizes these measures to preserve modesty (haya) and anatomical integrity during burial, reflecting the distinct fiqh rulings for female bodies in Shia jurisprudence. The practice underscores the importance of adhering to prophetic traditions in funeral rites while accommodating gender-specific physical characteristics.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of our companions, raising it, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about how the woman would be enshrouded. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Just as the man would be enshrouded, apart from that a cloth would be tightened upon her breasts to press the breasts upon the chest and it would be tightened upon her back, and the cotton (padding) would be done for her more than what would be done for the man, and stuffing the front and the back with the cotton and the embalming (camphor), then the cloth would be tightened upon her with an intense tightening’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from certain persons of our people in a marfu‘ manner who has said

the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about how must a woman be shrouded. He (the Imam) said, ‘A deceased woman is shrouded just like a deceased man, except that a piece of fabric is used to tie down her breasts to her chest, with the other end tied down behind her back. More cotton and camphor is used for hunut and to fill her back and front private parts and the piece of fabric is very tightly tied down around lower part of her body (as mentioned in the case of a deceased man).”
